newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: The Exxel Group buys Argentine supermarket chain.
newsitem.headline: The Exxel Group buys Argentine supermarket chain.

text.p: The international investment fund The Exxel Group announced Monday it bought all of Argentine supermarket chain CADESA (Supermercados Norte) for $440 million.
The purchase represents Argentina's biggest private company sale ever, an Exxel Group source told Reuters.
Supermercados Norte is the second largest Argentine supermarket by revenues, with annual sales of $1.3 billion, and is the largest vendor of food.
Supermercados Norte has 25 stores in Buenos Aires and the greater capital area.

Besides the $440 million paid for Supermercados Norte, The Exxel Group plans to invest in the chain $350 million over the next five years which will double the stores' staff to 13.000, the company official said.

The Exxel Group invests exclusively in companies in the customs union Mercosur formed by Argentina, Brazil, Paraguay and Uruguay. It controls several investment funds in which Rockefeller & Co, The Ford Foundation, The Getty Family Trust, CS First Boston, Credit Suisse Holdings, General Electric and Oppenheimer & Co. have stakes.
In the last four years The Exxel Group has invested $980 million in Argentina, mostly in private health, energy, restaurant and credit card sectors.
The official said the group has bought 19 companies with total annual revenues of $1.9 billion.
A formal announcement of the purchase is scheduled to be made at 1800 GMT by The Exxel Group head Juan Navarro and Supermercados Norte President Alberto Guil in the Buenos Aires Stock Exchange.
